newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumers shrug off price uptrend.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumers shrug off price uptrend.

text.p: German coffee roasters have enough near term cover to live with high nearby prices caused by low inventories and tightness at origin, traders said.
"Naturally it is annoying for some to be paying double-digit differentials for October/November premium coffees, but an end to the tightness is in sight," one said.
"Latin America's new crop will arrive here from the end of November onwards..this will ease the situation and most consumers can manage until then," he said.
Colombian differentials had already eased from 14/16 cents Sept/Oct to four to six cents for late November although those in the following months had not been established, traders said.
Central American sellers were closely watching developments in Colombia to set their own prices accordingly, traders said.
Brazil supplies also helped fill gaps in roasters' cover although their role as a substitute for Colombians and Central Americans in German blends is technically limited.

December arabica in New York ended at 109.80 per lb, a four-week high on the close, after widening its premium to the distant contracts to more than 6.00 cents last week, as a reflection of the tightness.
Robusta supplies, by comparison, looked comfortable as Vietnam's record 1996/97 crop was expected to offer ample follow-on business after Indonesia's ending harvest.
Vietnam expects to harvest 17 percent more this year, with an official earlier today putting the crop at 270,000 tonnes.
Traders also expected a relaxation of export taxes in Vietnam.
In the Bremen import market, Brazils were last offered at $108 per 50 kg fob, up $3 on the week, Colombia Excelso was at $126, up $2, and Indonesian robustas steady at $65.
